title: Ranks of Magi Bonisagi
heading: The Ranks of Magi Bonisagi
summary: Magi Bonisagi hold one of four research-based ranks, each with different duties and privileges (such as contributing a sigil to the Colentes pouch or being subject to the Primus's research commands). Rank is determined by House Acclaim.
quotes: There are four ranks for magi Bonisagi.
related: House Acclaim: Status in House Bonisagus

title: Colentes Arcanorum
heading: Colentes Arcanorum
summary: The five-member Bonisagus council, chosen at random from magi of cannophori rank or higher, that collects submitted Lab Texts and tractatus and compiles them into folios. Includes the chance that a character is selected and the council's powers over the Primus.
quotes: a player character who has achieved the rank of *cannophori* has a 1 in 5 chance of being selected

title: Submitted Texts (Colentes)
heading: Submitted Texts
summary: How many Lab Texts and tractatus a Colens receives during a term, what they look for, and how long it takes to judge a submission.
quotes: It takes a day for Colens Arcanorum to briefly scan a submitted text and determine its value.

title: Tenentes Occultorum
heading: Tenentes Occultorum
requires: House Bonisagus (magi Trianomae); Minor Status Virtue: Tenens Occultorum
summary: The four seasonal Trianomae officers who guard House secrets and watch mundane seekers of arcane lore, each responsible for a set of Tribunals. Explains how a character can begin play as a Tenens.
related: Ars Magica 5th Edition p.32 After Apprenticeship

title: Colloquium Delectorum
heading: Colloquium Delectorum
summary: The seven-yearly meeting at which the Colentes and Tenentes compile their findings, choose research for the next folio, and can be petitioned about the Primus's orders.

title: The Primus of House Bonisagus
heading: The Primus
summary: The Primus's powers (agenda-setting at Tribunals, selecting the councils, directing a magus's research) and the qualifications a candidate for Primus must meet.

title: Taking Another Magus's Apprentice
heading: Another Magus's Apprentice
summary: Magi of House Bonisagus alone may take another Hermetic magus's apprentice; the text lists informal House guidelines for using the right and the possible consequences (low crime charges, Wizard War), and notes that rank helps in finding an apprentice.
quotes: Unique among the Lineages, magi of House Bonisagus may take another Hermetic magus

title: Multiple Apprentices
heading: Multiple Apprentices
summary: Explains how many apprentices a magus can legally teach and the time cost, and gives magi Bonisagi the ability to use a second lab assistant so two apprentices can both assist in the lab.
quotes: magi Bonisagi can always successfully use a second lab assistant

title: Fostering Apprentices
heading: Fostering
summary: Magi Bonisagi swap apprentices for a year of Ability training and then a stint of lab assistance, a procedure that gives both apprentices Teaching and Profession: Scribe and improves Latin and Magic Theory.
quotes: At the end of two years, both apprentices should have scores of 2 in Teaching and Profession: Scribe, as well as improved scores in Latin and Magic Theory.

title: Optional Rule: Continuous Research
heading: Optional Rule: Continuous Research
summary: An optional storyguide rule that rewards a magus who stays uninterrupted on a single lab project by adding a growing bonus to the Lab Total as seasons accumulate; interruptions or a change of subject end the benefit.
quotes: Once you have spent five seasons on a project, accruing five Continual Research points, you may add 1 to your Lab Total.
related: ArM5 p.103 Distractions from Lab Work

title: Magic Theory Specializations of Magi Bonisagi
heading: Types of Magi Bonisagi
summary: Three optional Magic Theory specializations (traditionalist, dabbler, harmonizer) available only to magi Bonisagi, each applying when a particular kind of research, spell invention or enchantment is undertaken.
quotes: You may choose traditionalist, dabbler, or harmonizer as a specialization for your Magic Theory

title: Working Together (Bonisagus lab assistants)
heading: Working Together
requires: House Bonisagus (magi Bonisagi, their apprentices and familiars)
summary: Magi Bonisagi may have one more lab assistant than the normal rules allow, and the text explains when they are willing to act as assistants to other magi.
quotes: magi Bonisagi can always have one more lab assistant than the normal **ArM5** rules would allow a magus character to have

title: The Cipher of Trianoma
heading: The Cipher of Trianoma
requires: House Bonisagus (magi Trianomae); others may decode
summary: How magi of other lineages decipher the shorthand used by magi Trianomae, either by treating a cipher Lab Text as any other or by making a roll against a secret note.
quotes: To decode Trianoma's cipher you make an Intelligence + Latin + stress die roll.
Having decoded a previous cipher adds 3 to your decoding rolls.

title: House Acclaim: Status in House Bonisagus
heading: House Acclaim: Status in House Bonisagus
summary: A community-based Reputation that every magus Bonisagi starts with, which grows through finished and published laboratory research and moves the magus up the House ranks. Describes how Acclaim points accrue and are sped up by being included in a folio.
quotes: House Acclaim is a free Reputation that every magus Bonisagi character receives at character generation.
The lucky author gains twice the Acclaim points listed on the following table if his research is included in a folio.

title: Research and Acclaim Points
heading: Research and Acclaim Points
summary: Table of how many Acclaim points each kind of laboratory achievement (tractatus, summae, spells, talismans, familiars, apprentices, Breakthroughs and so on) is worth, with a note on how rank affects fostering and gauntlets.
quotes: Write an Art tractatus
Stabilize a Breakthrough

title: House Acclaim Points and Score
heading: House Acclaim Points and Score
summary: Table converting Acclaim points into an Acclaim score and rank title, plus the uses of the score: social bonuses within the House, a bonus to resist magi Trianomae, and a bonus to the roll to find an apprentice.
quotes: to any social skill roll involving her Presence characteristic when interacting with another magus of House Bonisagus
You may add your Acclaim score to your roll to find an apprentice

title: Folios
heading: Folios
summary: What a folio is, when and where the Colentes Arcanorum compile it, and how it is copied and circulated through the Order.
quotes: Folios are collections of Laboratory Texts and tractatus compiled by the Colentes Arcanorum

title: Writing Folios
heading: Writing Folios
summary: Procedure and capacity limit for creating a folio in a season, based on the Colentes' combined Magic Theory, plus how much each Colens can copy, with a worked example.
quotes: The Colentes Arcanorum's combined Magic Theory scores are the maximum total of Lab Text magnitudes and tractatus Qualities that can be included in a single volume.
Folios: Colentes combined Magic Theory = Sum of Lab Text magnitudes and/or tractatus Qualities
A Colens may copy 12 magnitudes of Lab Texts per point in Profession: Scribe into a folio.

title: Reading Folios
heading: Reading Folios
summary: Each text in a folio is studied like a stand-alone text, and finishing one earns a small Order of Hermes Lore bonus.
quotes: Each individual Lab Text or tractatus must be read for an entire season, just as if it was a stand alone text.
you receive one experience point in Order of Hermes Lore

title: Editorial Disagreements
heading: Editorial Disagreements
summary: Optional contest rolled between characters who argue over which texts go into a folio, using Presence + Leadership or Communication + Artes Liberales plus House Acclaim.
quotes: Loud characters may make a Presence + Leadership stress roll.
Crafty characters may make a Communication + Artes Liberales stress roll.

title: Copying Folios
heading: Copying Folios
summary: Rate at which a scribe copies a folio carefully or quickly, and the penalty to tractatus Quality for quick copying.
quotes: If a scribe is copying a folio carefully, he accumulates points equal to 6 + his Profession: Scribe score in a season.
If he copies the folio quickly, he gains 18 + 3 times his Profession: Scribe score in accumulated points per season.

title: Intrigue Rolls (Magi Trianomae)
heading: Copying Folios
summary: The Intrigue subsection has lost its own heading in this file and follows Copying Folios (from line 782). It gives rolls and Ease Factors for influencing or interrogating an NPC with Intrigue, the Gift penalty, and the contested form between two active participants with a table of results by margin of victory.
quotes: Influence a non-player character: Presence + Intrigue vs. variable Ease Factor
Interrogate a non-player character: Communication + Intrigue vs. variable Ease Factor
the magus Trianomae rolls Presence + Intrigue + a stress die against the target's Communication + Intrigue + stress die

title: Folk Ken and Guile
heading: Folk Ken and Guile
summary: Guidance for secret Folk Ken rolls to read an important NPC, how Guile counters them, and how Folk Ken feeds a bonus or penalty to Intrigue rolls at a Tribunal.
quotes: the storyguide may make a secret Per + Folk Ken roll
A character attempting to deceive rolls Com + Guile.

title: Original Research
heading: Original Research
summary: Introduction to original research, the process by which a magus tries to push the limits of Hermetic magic; notes that anyone can start at any time with no minimum Art or Ability.
quotes: There are no minimum Art or Ability requirements for undertaking original research

title: Breakthroughs
heading: Breakthroughs
summary: Defines the three kinds of Breakthrough (Minor, Major, Hermetic), with examples of each, and advises discussing the target with the troupe first.
quotes: These achievements are called **Breakthroughs** and there are three types: Minor, Major, and Hermetic.

title: Seeking the Unknown
heading: Seeking the Unknown
summary: First stage of original research: experiment with a spell or enchantment to roll a Discovery on the Extraordinary Results Chart, using a Magic Theory-limited risk modifier applied to the roll rather than the Lab Total.
quotes: For every five points or fraction thereof of Magic Theory (including Puissant Magic Theory) you may choose a risk modifier of 1.
Risk Modifier: +1 per 5 points of Magic Theory or fraction thereof, up to +3
Breakthrough: roll Discovery on the Extraordinary Results Chart during a season of Arcane Experimentation

title: Stabilizing the Unknown
heading: Stabilizing the Unknown
summary: Second stage of original research: repeat the Discovery experiment exactly, with the same Lab Total, risk modifier use, vis and seasons, and avoid a harmful result to turn it into Breakthrough points and a Lab Text. Also covers the Warping Points gained from the attempt.
quotes: As long as you do not roll a harmful effect (Disaster, No Benefit, Complete Failure) you stabilize your discovery.
Magnitudes of Stabilized Discovery equal Breakthrough points

title: Warping Points from Stabilizing a Discovery
heading: Warping Points gained: the Magnitude of the Stabilized Discovery minus a simple die
summary: Warping Points are gained whether stabilization succeeds or fails, and a failed stabilization may be retried in consecutive seasons.
quotes: Warping Points gained: the Magnitude of the Stabilized Discovery minus a simple die
You receive Warping Points whether you succeed or fail at stabilizing your discovery.

title: Surpassing the Limits
heading: Surpassing the Limits
summary: When accumulated stabilized-discovery points reach a secret target set by the storyguide, a Breakthrough is achieved; gives a rule-of-thumb target by Breakthrough type and explains why the player should not know it.
quotes: A rough rule of thumb is 30 points are needed for a Minor Breakthrough, 45 for a Major and 60 for a true Hermetic Breakthrough.

title: Multiple Laboratory Texts (Collaborative Research)
heading: Multiple Laboratory Texts
summary: How a magus can add another magus's original-research Lab Texts to their own Breakthrough points by reading them for a season in a laboratory, without gaining Warping Points; the first researcher to reach the target makes the Breakthrough.
quotes: You accumulate points equal to your Lab Total in the Arts concerned.

title: Breakthroughs in Play
heading: Breakthroughs in Play
summary: How a completed Minor, Major or Hermetic Breakthrough is used and passed on to other magi (through a spell, personal teaching, tractatus, or as an Arcane Ability).
quotes: You do not have to subtract your total Hermetic Arts score from the Source Quality of the teaching source.

title: Hermetic Integration
heading: Hermetic Integration
summary: Explains how a further Breakthrough on a Major Breakthrough can fold its Virtue into ordinary Hermetic magic so that it no longer needs to be learned separately.

title: Exempli Gratia: Original Research
heading: Exempli Gratia: Original Research
summary: A worked example following a magus through experiments, a Discovery roll with a risk modifier, and the stabilization season.

title: Arma Magica (Parma Folds)
heading: Arma Magica
summary: Introduces the Arma Magica folds as Major Breakthroughs built on Parma Magica, and limits how many folds a magus can know and how many students can be taught a fold.
quotes: A magus may know a number of folds equal to his Parma Magica score.

title: Parma Magica Folds
heading: Parma Magica Folds
summary: Rules for calculating magic resistance under the folds, and descriptions of the Ablativa, Absorbea, Condensa, Custodia, Repercussa and Restricta variants of Parma Magica with their effects, casting times and restrictions.
quotes: Double a magus's Parma Magica score when calculating magic resistance.
Double the Parma Magica score against the specified Form, but divide it by two (round up) against all others.
The magus adds twice his Parma Magica score to any Defense totals in combat.

title: Parmulae
heading: Parmulae
summary: A lesser enchanted device giving its wearer fixed magic resistance for a limited time, with its construction cost, level of effect and limitations, plus a warning to discuss it with the troupe.
quotes: Parmulae: Lesser Enchanted Device that provides a magic resistance of 30. Total level of effect is 44.
Its base level of effect is Rego Vim 30.

title: Figurine Magic
heading: Figurine Magic
summary: Procedure for crafting and enchanting short-lived wax or wood figurines for a single recipient, giving them a Minor Virtue or a Hermetic spell, with construction rolls, enchantment Ease Factors, and limits on which Virtues can be imbued.
quotes: Constructing a figurine takes a month for a wax figurine or two for a wood figurine.
Making a figure: Dexterity + Craft: Sculptor + Stress die
Enchanting a figure: Intelligence + Figurine Magic +Aura Modifier

title: Realm-Aligned Spells
heading: Realm-Aligned Spells
requires: Saga option: Realm-Aligned Spell Minor Breakthrough
summary: How to invent a spell flavored to the Magic, Faerie or Infernal realm so it is immune to that realm's normal interaction and rolls fewer botch dice, at the cost of a lower Lab Total during invention.
quotes: you reduce your Lab Total by limiting your Magic Theory Ability score to the level of your appropriate Realm Lore

title: Realm-Aligned Spell Interaction Table
heading: Realm-Aligned Spell Interaction Table
requires: Saga option: Realm-Aligned Spell Minor Breakthrough
summary: Table giving the aura bonus or penalty applied to a realm-aligned spell by aura type and spell flavor, replacing the normal Realm Interaction Table.

title: Becoming a Quaesitor
heading: Becoming a Quaesitor
summary: How a magus of any House is selected, mentored and appointed as a Quaesitor, and which Abilities the training and exposure covers in game terms.
quotes: In game terms this gives the candidate training and exposure to, Code of Hermes, Hermes Lore, Awareness, Folk Ken and Intrigue.

title: Tribunals and the First Tribunal
heading: Tribunals
summary: Distinguishes the First Tribunal from the regional and Grand Tribunals, which matters for the hierarchy of Tribunal rulings.

title: Magvillus Council
heading: The Magvillus Council
summary: Composition, quorum and decision rules of the inner and outer tiers of the council that governs House Guernicus and sits in judgment on wider matters.
quotes: An attendance of twenty-one is considered quorum.

title: The Law in Your Saga
heading: The Law in Your Saga
summary: Advice to troupes on how strictly the Code is enforced, how strong the Traditionalist and Transitionalist factions are, and how uniform Tribunals are in their saga.

title: Forfeit Immunity
heading: Forfeit Immunity
summary: The key defense against Hermetic charges: a magus may lose legal protection in a Wizard War or while committing a crime, and the response must be proportional.
quotes: This lack of legal protection is called forfeit immunity.
While forfeit other magi may act against him, but the response should be proportional.

title: The Hermetic Oath (Interpretation)
heading: The Hermetic Oath
summary: Explains that the following sections present a condensed Traditionalist reading of the First Tribunal rulings and that the Presiding Quaesitor is the authority on the Code.
quotes: The Presiding Quaesitor is the authority on the Code

title: High and Low Crimes
heading: High and Low Crimes
summary: Lists the high crimes under the Code and explains that only a high crime allows the prosecution to call for a Wizard's March; all other offenses are low crimes.
quotes: If the case is a high crime, the prosecution can call for a Wizard's March, otherwise he cannot.

title: Deprivation of Magical Power
heading: Deprivation of Magical Power
summary: What counts as depriving a magus of magical power, including injuries, vis, sites, items, familiars, apprentices, books and lab equipment.

title: Slaying a Magus
heading: Slaying
summary: The prohibition on slaying a member of the Order, the defenses of forfeit immunity and sanctum intrusion, and sample Tribunal rulings.
quotes: being within another's sanctum automatically confers forfeit immunity with respect to the owner of the sanctum

title: Amici
heading: Amici
summary: The custom of sworn friendship between magi and the lasting moral duty to avenge an amicus, relevant before declaring a Wizard War.

title: Wizard War
heading: Wizard War
summary: The legal procedure and limits of a Wizard War: delivery of the declaration, the time to prepare and the duration, what property may be attacked, immunity from prosecution, and sample rulings.
quotes: the recipient of the declaration has a lunar month to prepare and then the war lasts for a lunar month
A magus cannot legally attack property in which his opponent has shared ownership, such as covenant buildings, vis sites and covenant books.

title: Abide by Tribunal Decisions
heading: Abide by Tribunal Decisions
summary: Whose rulings bind whom: regional Tribunal rulings apply to residents and visitors, First and Grand Tribunal rulings apply everywhere, and regional rulings may not contradict higher ones.
quotes: A regional Tribunal cannot rule in contradiction to First and Grand Tribunal rulings.

title: Proxy Voting
heading: Proxy Voting
summary: How a magus can give his sigil to another magus to vote for him at Tribunal, the difference between directed and free proxies, the obligation to report the vote, and the Tremere practice of holding filii's sigils.
quotes: A magus can give his sigil to an attending magus who agrees to act as proxy.
Not following the instructions is a high crime.

title: Voting Rights and Residency
heading: Voting Rights
summary: Each magus's single vote at their residential and the Grand Tribunal, how residency is chosen and changed, delinquent residency, and the duty to vote prudently.
quotes: Each magus must have a single Tribunal of residence.
Such a magus has seven years to meet the requirements or join another Tribunal.

title: Vagrancy
heading: Vagrancy
summary: The legal requirement to belong to a House, the time allowed to find a new one after leaving or being expelled, how sponsorship works, and vagrancy for lacking a residential Tribunal.
quotes: Magi who renounce their House membership or are expelled have one year to obtain membership in another.

title: Endangerment
heading: Endangerment
summary: The Hermetic Oath provision against endangering the Order, what the prosecution must show, and how intent and negligence affect the penalty.
quotes: The prosecution needs to show that magi other than the defendant were endangered.

title: Mundane Interference
heading: Mundane Interference
summary: The prohibition on interfering in mundane affairs, what it forbids, and how a magus in conflict with a mundane can stay within the law.

title: Deals with Devils
heading: Deals with Devils
summary: The most strictly enforced high crime: knowingly making an agreement with an infernal agent, the only defense of ignorance, the legality of hunting demons, and a sample ruling.
quotes: Magi are absolutely forbidden from knowingly making an agreement with an infernal agent.

title: Molesting the Fay
heading: Molesting the Fay
summary: What the prosecution must show for a charge of molesting the fay and the defense of reasonable self-protection.
quotes: The prosecution will have to show that a magus or covenant has endangered other magi.

title: Scrying on Members of the Order
heading: Scrying
summary: What counts as illegal scrying on other magi, the legality of detection magics in a covenant, and the special protection of Redcaps and use of spells without Penetration.
quotes: The key point is 'legal affairs'.

title: Apprentices under the Code
heading: Apprentices
summary: When an apprenticeship legally begins, how an unclaimed Gifted child can be taken, and how adult non-Hermetic wizards join the Order and are sponsored.
quotes: To officially claim an apprentice a magus must initiate them into Hermetic magic.

title: Duty of the Parens
heading: Duty of the Parens
summary: The parens's duty to strike down an apprentice who turns against the Order, who inherits the duty, and the legal consequences of failing to carry it out.
quotes: The Oath demands the parens be the first to attack an outcast magus.

title: Bonisagus Rights and Duties
heading: Bonisagus Rights and Duties
summary: Oath provisions requiring Bonisagus magi to share their discoveries and Lab Texts and requiring other magi to concede Bonisagus's right to take their apprentices, with a sample ruling.

title: Casting Out
heading: Casting Out
summary: How a convicted magus who refuses the offered lesser punishment is cast out of the Order.
quotes: If taken literally, all convictions should lead to a Wizard's March.

title: Enemies and Allies of the Order
heading: Enemies and Allies
summary: Magi who aid enemies or attack friends and allies of the Order may be prosecuted; only a Tribunal can declare an enemy.
quotes: Only a Tribunal can declare an individual or group as an enemy

title: The Peripheral Code and Case Rulings
heading: The Peripheral Code
summary: Explains that Tribunal rulings together form the Peripheral Code and how earlier case rulings are used by prosecution and defense.
quotes: There are two types of Tribunal ruling, case and proposed.

title: The Legality of Certamen
heading: The Legality of Certamen
summary: Legal limits on Certamen: it cannot be used to defy a Tribunal judgment, force a Code breach or hide a violation, and a mutually accepted challenge cannot be appealed.
quotes: Certamen could not be used to defy a Tribunal judgment, make a magus break the Code or ignore a Code violation.
If a challenge is mutually accepted no Tribunal appeal is possible.

title: Proposal Rulings
heading: Proposal Rulings
summary: How a magus proposes a new Tribunal ruling, how far in advance it must be published, and how popular rulings spread to other Tribunals.
quotes: Proposals need to be published no later than two years prior to the Tribunal.

title: The Detail of the Peripheral Code
heading: The Detail
summary: Guidance on inventing Tribunal rulings and a list of the kinds of matters the Peripheral Code normally covers.

title: Determining the Principals
heading: Determining the Principals
summary: Who becomes prosecution and defense principal in a case, and the order of precedence among volunteers.
quotes: In descending order these are: parens, filius, amicus, covenant sodales and then any other magus.

title: Determining the Tribunal
heading: Determining the Tribunal
summary: Rules for deciding which Tribunal hears a case, including border regions, duty to give one's name and residence, and who bears travel costs.
quotes: In all other situations, the case should be brought to the defendant's Tribunal.

title: Apprentices of House Bonisagus
heading: Apprentices
summary: How House Bonisagus apprentices are chosen and trained, and the distinct gauntlets of the two branches: the Theoretical Interview for magi Bonisagi and a solo journey for magi Trianomae.

title: Publishing a Case
heading: Publishing a Case
summary: The prosecuting principal must notify the defendant, Presiding Quaesitor and Praeco in advance, usually through Redcaps; later-discovered crimes are heard only if the defendant attends.
quotes: This should be done no later than three months prior to the Tribunal.

title: Lawful Tyranny
heading: Lawful Tyranny
summary: A defendant may legally threaten Wizard War to make a prosecutor drop a case; transferring the case to a powerful principal or a Guernicus advocate is the usual counter.
quotes: A prosecuting principal can always transfer a case before publishing it.

title: Transferring a Case
heading: Transferring a Case
summary: Either principal may hand their case to an advocate; covers the share of fines paid to a prosecution principal and the duty to prepare consistent witness testimony.
quotes: A successful prosecution can net substantial fines, a third of which go to the prosecution principal.

title: Private Hearing
heading: Private Hearing
summary: The first stage of presenting a case: both principals summarize in private before the Presiding Quaesitor, who may rule on disputed facts, give an opinion and offer a summary judgment only if both sides agree.
quotes: The Presiding Quaesitor cannot offer a summary judgment unless both the defense and prosecution principal agree to it.

title: Public Hearing
heading: Public Hearing
summary: The order of presentation, witness testimony, perjury challenges and voting at a full Tribunal hearing, decided by a simple majority with the Praeco breaking ties.
quotes: A simple majority decides, with the Praeco breaking any ties.

title: Acquittal
heading: Acquittal
summary: After an acquittal the prosecution principal covers the defense principal's costs, and any counter-case begins immediately with roles reversed.
quotes: If a case ends in an acquittal the prosecution principal is liable for all the defense principal's costs.

title: Conviction
heading: Conviction
summary: After a conviction for a high crime the prosecution may call for a Wizard's March, voted by simple majority with a tie defeating the motion; otherwise the Presiding Quaesitor offers a lesser penalty.
quotes: A simple majority decides, with a tie defeating the motion.

title: Testimony
heading: Testimony
summary: Rules for giving testimony in person or in writing, perjury challenges and the Presiding Quaesitor's veto of them, Quaesitorial endorsement, and testimony of testimony.
quotes: No magus can be forced to submit to truth-detection spells.

title: Counter-Case Example
heading: Counter-Case Example
summary: Worked example of two magi who each charge the other over a vis source, showing how an acquittal triggers an immediate counter-case.

title: Damages
heading: Damages
summary: Damages are paid directly to the victim, including costs of the case, and in a March the victim normally receives a share of the outcast's estate.
quotes: the Presiding Quaesitor will normally grant the victim one quarter of the outcast's estate

title: Fines
heading: Fines
summary: How fines are divided between the prosecutor and the Tribunal coffers, and how a March splits the outcast's estate.
quotes: one third is given to the prosecutor, two-thirds to the Tribunal coffers

title: Determining Penalties
heading: Determining Penalties
summary: How the Presiding Quaesitor sets compensation and punishment, the convicted magus's options (accept, negotiate, refuse), payment deadlines, and appeal to Magvillus.
quotes: If the magus refuses a lesser penalty three times the Quaesitor will declare the magus Marched.
Damages, fines or services should normally be paid or completed in full by the next Tribunal.

title: Wizard's March
heading: Wizard's March
summary: What it means to be cast out of the Order: outlaw status, the parens's duty, the sanctity of Tribunal grounds and the usual grace period before the outcast can be attacked.
quotes: Normally, magi that the Tribunal has voted to cast out have until the end of the Tribunal before they can be legally attacked.

title: Punishments (Hierarchy)
heading: Punishments
summary: Introduces the ladder of Hermetic punishments from seasons of service up to the death of a familiar. This is the second heading named Punishments (the first, at line 1901, is a one-line overview).
quotes: Punishments are set in a hierarchy to accord with the seriousness of the conviction.

title: Seasons of Service
heading: Seasons of Service
summary: A convicted magus performs seasons of work for Mercere or Guernicus magi in support of their Tribunal duties, such as longevity rituals, invested devices or copying records.
quotes: The Presiding Quaesitor normally splits the seasons in the favor of Mercere magi.

title: Investing Items (Punishment)
heading: Investing Items
summary: The magus must invest items with negotiated effects and deliver them to Mercere or Guernicus members.

title: Loss of an Apprentice
heading: Loss of an Apprentice
summary: The convicted magus surrenders their apprentice; the prosecuting principal has first claim and certamen settles competing candidates.
quotes: If multiple suitable candidates step forward, certamen contests decide the matter.

title: Banishment from Tribunal
heading: Banishment from Tribunal
summary: The magus must avoid the Tribunal's area, arrange others to harvest any vis sources there, and find a new residential Tribunal.
quotes: The magus is required to find another residential Tribunal.

title: Loss of Familiar
heading: Loss of Familiar
summary: The cords binding magus and familiar are cut by a Quaesitorial ritual or a season of lab work, and the former familiar normally cannot be rebound.
quotes: The former familiar cannot normally be rebound.

title: Death of Familiar
heading: Death of Familiar
summary: The harshest punishment short of a March: the familiar is killed, and some magi choose a March instead.
quotes: The convicted magus's familiar must be killed.

title: Quaesitor in Good Standing
heading: Quaesitor in Good Standing
summary: A Quaesitor needs a current signed letter from the Guernicus Primus to have authority to demand cooperation or preside at Tribunal.
quotes: This letter must be less than seven years old to be valid.

title: Investigation Duties
heading: Investigation Duties
summary: A Quaesitor must investigate serious complaints but is entitled to seasons of his own each year, which may be accrued.
quotes: He is also entitled to at least three seasons every year to pursue his own studies or attend to covenant responsibilities.

title: Cooperation with Investigations
heading: Cooperation
summary: By Grand Tribunal ruling, magi must cooperate with an official investigation and let their servants be questioned, but need not reveal legal magical secrets.
quotes: Failure to cooperate with an investigation is a low crime.

title: Investigation Immunity
heading: Investigation Immunity
requires: Quaesitor (or an agent) in a justified investigation
summary: Limits on when a Quaesitor may use Intellego magic in investigations without breaching the scrying prohibition, what liability remains for incidental discoveries, and who else the immunity covers.
quotes: However, Intellego Mentem magic can never be used on magi or their servants without their permission.
related: Scrying on Members of the Order

title: Sanctum Invasions
heading: Sanctum Invasions
summary: A Quaesitor may enter a sanctum under investigation, during which time they are under forfeit immunity, though investigation immunity protects them from charges about the invasion.
quotes: While within the sanctum, the Quaesitor and any of their agents are under forfeit immunity.

title: Compensation for Quaesitors
heading: Compensation
summary: How vis spent on an investigation and a seasonal rate are repaid from Tribunal coffers or by an unfounded complainant, and the share of fines for a Quaesitor who also prosecutes.
quotes: Three pawns per season is a typical figure, but this will vary between sagas and Tribunals.

title: Calling a Wizard's March
heading: Calling a Wizard's March
summary: A Quaesitor can declare a March outside Tribunal for an immediate threat such as a diabolist; the next Tribunal reviews it and the Quaesitor may not profit from it.
quotes: By Grand Tribunal ruling, no Quaesitor can materially benefit in any way from calling a Wizard's March.

title: Consultation and Arbitration
heading: Consultation and Arbitration
summary: Quaesitors may draft and witness agreements or arbitrate disputes; an arbitrated agreement is binding by Grand Tribunal ruling.
quotes: Once agreed, failure to comply with this agreement is an offense by Grand Tribunal ruling.

title: The Presiding Quaesitor
heading: The Presiding Quaesitor
summary: How a Presiding Quaesitor is chosen, the role of his two advisers, his powers of veto and appeal to the Grand Tribunal, and the vote to validate a Tribunal.
quotes: He then calls for a vote to validate the Tribunal, which requires a twothirds majority.

title: Endorsing Testimony
heading: Endorsing Testimony
summary: How a Quaesitor magically verifies testimony: the witness lowers all defenses, the Quaesitor checks for manipulation, and conflicting endorsed testimony raises suspicion of infernal involvement.
quotes: the Quaesitor endorsing the testimony must be senior to or at least a peer of the witness

title: The Veto
heading: The Veto
summary: When a Presiding Quaesitor may veto a ruling, how a veto is reviewed by Magvillus and appealed to the Grand Tribunal, and a suggested troupe roll to judge a clear conflict with the Code.
quotes: This is a very limited judgment, requiring an Int + Code of Hermes roll of 6+ to determine.
